name: ShaderScene
label: Shader scene
description: A WebGL2 scene in the theme's field colours: a night horizon, rift, meteors, aurora, underwater, embers, snow or pastel, with fades and grain.

props.name: scene
props.description: The scene to paint: `horizon`, a planet's limb at night, `rift`, a glowing tear, `glyphs`, soft light printed in type, `prism`, beams of light split into a spectrum, `meteors`, a shower over a planet's edge, `waves`, a rolling sea of points, or `aurora`, ribbons of colour round a void, `underwater`, caustic light over deep water with sunbeams and rising bubbles, `embers`, sparks rising off a low hearth, `snow`, snow falling through a dark sky over a bank, `pastel`, soft washes laid on in slow brushed strokes, `rocket`, stars streaking out from a vanishing point over a hot exhaust, or `sunset`, a sun setting into a calm sea with its reflection on the water.

props.name: params
props.description:
The scene's settings, merged over its defaults (`SHADER_SCENES` lists each
scene's keys and ranges), so passing one changes one thing. Changing them
never rebuilds the GL state.

props.name: passes
props.description:
The finishing passes (`scrim`, `vignette`, `fadeTop`, `fadeBottom`,
`grain`), each merged over its defaults.

props.name: speed
props.description: Scene seconds per second: how fast it moves. 0 holds it still.

props.name: liveRef
props.description:
A ref the scene reads every frame in place of `params`, `passes` and
`speed`, for a host that tunes it by drag: writing the ref moves the
scene and renders nothing. Empty falls back to the props.

props.name: enabled
props.description:
False never starts WebGL and reports `unavailable`, painting nothing:
the kill switch, as on ShaderField.

props.name: onStatusChange
props.description:
Called whenever the status changes. Drive a fallback from this, or lay
one under the scene: it paints nothing until it is `active`, so what
shows while it is pending or cannot run is the caller's design
decision.

ShaderScenePassSetting.description: One finishing pass's setting: whether it runs, and its own settings.

ShaderSceneStatus.description:
How the scene resolved, the same three states ShaderField reports.
`pending` while the GL context comes up (bounded by a watchdog), `active`
once a frame has painted, `unavailable` when it is disabled or WebGL2
cannot run it.

Values.description: What the canvas reads every frame. A ref holds it, so a drag never renders.
